After expanding every local definition to primitives I found no printed sub-clause of lem:carriers (i)-(iv) without a Lean counterpart, no Lean clause weaker than the printed one, no added hypothesis, and no local definition that fails to denote the printed object. Verdict: not refuted (faithful, with the Lean stronger in several places).

DOMAIN. `carriers_lemma (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hP : Generic P) (hS : IsDecomposition hn hP S)` (statement lines 127-128). `Generic = G1 ∧ G2` (Generic.lean): G1 = every distinct vertex triple has chi ≠ 0, G2 = no three edge interiors concur — exactly source lines 2-4. `IsDecomposition = S ∈ independentSupports` = `∀ x y ∈ S, x ≠ y → ¬Interlaces` (DecompositionDefinition.lean) — source line 11-12. The only extra argument is the typeclass `[NeZero n]`, implied by 3 ≤ n; harmless.

MODEL. `Mark P = ZMod n ⊕ Visit P` (every original vertex and every crossing visit, source 97-98); `markPosition` = (i,0) for vertices, `visitPosition = (edge, crossingParameter)` for visits, sorted by `traversalKey = i.val + t` — the def:gauss order cut at label 0; `markSuccessor = ρ` = cyclic next in that list; `smoothingSuccessor S = ρ ∘ selectedMarkPerm S`, i.e. `ρ_S(a) = ρ(b)` at a selected pair, identity elsewhere (`smoothingSuccessor_visit_of_mem/_not_mem`, `_vertex`) — source eq. carrierpr:successors 104-106; `Component` = SameCycle-quotient of ρ_S, `owner a = ⟦a⟧` — source 109-112 ("node a retains its incoming arc"; I verified ρ_S⁻¹(a) = selectedMarkPerm(ρ⁻¹ a) has the same plane point as ρ⁻¹ a and lies in a's cycle, so a's cycle contains the incoming one-sided arc at a: conv:selected-visits). `smoothingSegment a u = eval(a) + u·(eval(ρ_S a) − eval(a))` is the inherited straight subsegment from a to ρ_S a; at a selected a it runs from the crossing point along b's outgoing subsegment to ρ(b) (source 193-197). ρ_S is defined from S alone, so "independent of the order of reconnections" is structural; the library additionally has `selectedMarkPerm_commute` / `smoothingSuccessor_union_of_disjoint` showing sequential processing yields the same permutation. I judge that sufficient.

(i) `count`: Fintype.card Component = |S|+1 ✓. `component_cycle`: componentCycle q = markCycle.filter (owner = q) — definitional (rfl), the owner-filtered marked circle in inherited order. `inherited_order`: `InheritsMarkOrder S = ∀ q a ∈ componentCycle q, (componentCycle q).next a = ρ_S a` — the carrier's actual successor is the inherited-next owned mark; STRONGER than printed (all marks, not just visits). `selected_visits_separated` ✓ verbatim.

(ii) `corner_polygons`: `ccpCornerList = componentMarkList.filter IsTrueCorner` (owned marks in inherited order, kept if original vertex or selected visit), `ccpCornerPolygon j = eval(ccpCornerList[j])`. Conjuncts: trace-set equality ⋃ σ_a([0,1]) = ⋃ edgeSegment(ccp) (extra, STRONGER), edge ≠ 0 and = c·d_e with c>0 (nonzero edges; positive multiples of original directions — proof 199-201, STRONGER), 3 ≤ corners, no antiparallel consecutive, Regular (= ∀ i, edge ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, edge i = r·edge(i−1), def:regular), all turns ≠ 0, vertex corner turn = turn P i = τ_i (def:chirotope), selected corner at v has turn = crossingSign P v.2 (twin v).2 = sgn det(d_i,d_j) with i the incoming edge (proof 206-207), twin has sgn det(d_j,d_i), opposite and one ±1 each ✓.

(iii) Parametrisation: `IsCarrierParameter q (a,u) = owner a = q ∧ 0 ≤ u < 1`, `carrierTrace (a,u) = smoothingSegment a u`. The closed curve of q is ⋃_{owner a = q} σ_a([0,1]); since σ_a(1) = σ_{ρ_S a}(0) (`smoothingSegment_glue`) and owner(ρ_S a) = owner a, every point is reached with u ∈ [0,1), and the half-open pieces are a bijective parametrisation of the abstract traversal cycle. So "two distinct parameters" = "passed at two distinct times" = self-intersection, "three distinct parameters" = triple point. ρ_S has no fixed points and all segments are non-degenerate (remote edges are separated by a vertex mark), so no spurious same-mark coincidences. Complete and once-except-at-self-intersections: ✓. `self_intersections` conj.1: IsSelfIntersection q x ↔ ∃ c ∈ carrierCrossings q, x = crossingPoint c, with `carrierCrossings q = {x ∉ S | ∀ v, v.1 = x → owner (inr v) = q}` — exactly "unselected crossings both of whose visits are assigned to it" (def:smoothing 24-25) ✓ ("exactly" is the iff, both directions). Transverse (conj.2): for both visits w of c, det(d_{w.2}, d_{twin.2}) ≠ 0, the outgoing carrier segment at w is a positive multiple of d_{w.2}, at twin w a positive multiple of d_{twin.2}, and the two outgoing segment vectors have det ≠ 0 — transversality of the "unchanged straight germs" (proof 234). The incoming germs are not restated in the lemma; they are supplied by the accepted def:smoothing row `SmoothingData.unselected_visit_straight` (incoming and outgoing pieces at an unselected visit lie on the visited edge, positive direction), so the two branches are straight lines through x with independent directions. I flag this as the one place the rendering relies on an accepted row rather than restating; it is not a missing sub-clause. Not a corner (conj.3): crossingPoint c ≠ any P k, ≠ any selected crossing point, the visits of c are not IsTrueCorner (redundant with c ∉ S), and ∀ m, IsTrueCorner S m → eval(m) ≠ crossingPoint c. Since the corners of every carrier are exactly its IsTrueCorner marks (`ccpCornerMark`), this gives ∀ q j, ccpCornerPolygon q j ≠ x — STRONGER (all carriers), and exactly the printed proof's reading (235-236: "original vertices and selected crossing sites are all distinct from it"). No triple point (conj.4): ∀ x, ¬IsTriplePoint q x, for every q ✓; not vacuous since IsCarrierParameter is satisfiable and complete. Ownership: `neighbor_visits_separated` over x ∈ supportNeighbors = N(S) = {y | ∃ x ∈ S, Interlaces y x} (Interlaces = alternating visits, def:interlace) ✓ (under independence N(S) ∩ S = ∅, so "unselected" is automatic; otherwise Lean is stronger); `nonneighbor_visits_together` over x ∈ supportUnselected = univ \ (S ∪ N(S)) = U(S) ✓.

Faithful to source lines 35-37; selected visits included ✓. Not vacuous: visitPosition is injective and the order is total.
